info.title: Pulumi Cloud API (baton-pulumi-cloud connector surface)
info.description:
Describes only the Pulumi Cloud endpoints baton-pulumi-cloud calls. Scope is derived from pkg/client/client.go; response shapes are derived from the structs in that same file and settled against Pulumi's live OpenAPI document at https://api.pulumi.com/api/openapi/pulumi-spec.json (accessed 2026-09-23).

Only the properties the connector's structs declare are modelled. Pulumi's document describes many more per resource; the omissions are deliberate — spec scope is connector scope.

Auth: a Pulumi access token sent as `Authorization: token <token>`. Note the scheme keyword is the literal string `token`, not `Bearer`.

Pagination: only listOrganizationMembers paginates. It returns an opaque `continuationToken`; the connector replays it as the `continuationToken` query parameter and stops once the field is absent. listTeams and getTeam return complete collections with no pagination.

Base URL: https://api.pulumi.com by default, overridable via the connector's base-URL config. Every path is prefixed `/api` by buildURL.

servers.description: Pulumi Cloud API. Default; overridable via the connector's base-url config.

get.summary: List the members of an organization
get.description:
Source of the connector's user resources (pkg/connector/user.go:71) and of the organization role grants (pkg/connector/org.go:93). Also the connector's credential-validation probe, called with an empty continuation token (pkg/connector/connector.go:44).

The client hardcodes `type=backend` on every call. This is load-bearing, not boilerplate: Pulumi documents this route as having two distinct modes and defaults to `frontend` when the parameter is omitted. A backend member is the organization's identity-provider-backed membership (GitHub, GitLab, or for SAML orgs the Pulumi database); a frontend member is the Pulumi-database membership counted against the seat cap. Dropping the parameter changes which people the connector syncs.

`user.githubLogin` is the connector's user resource ID and the `userLogin` path parameter for every write — parity-critical.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Which member list to return. The connector always sends `backend`. Pulumi defaults to `frontend` when omitted, which would return a different set of people.

parameters.name: continuationToken
parameters.description: Opaque page cursor, echoed back from the previous response's `continuationToken`. Omitted on the first call.

patch.description:
Backs both the organization role grant (pkg/connector/org.go:153) and the demotion half of revoke: revoking `admin` sets the role back to `member` rather than removing the person (pkg/connector/org.go:182).

The connector only ever sends `admin` or `member`. Pulumi accepts a wider enum and also supports a custom-role form via `fgaRoleId`, which the connector does not use.

Pulumi returns 204 with no body; the client discards the response.

404.description: User not found in the organization.

delete.summary: Remove a member from the organization
delete.description:
Backs revoking the `member` entitlement (pkg/connector/org.go:185). Pulumi also drops the user from every team in the organization as a side effect, so team grants disappear without the connector issuing a team write.

Pulumi rejects self-removal with a 400. The client sends no body and decodes no response.

400.description: The caller cannot remove themselves from the organization.

404.description: User not found in the organization.

get.summary: List the teams in an organization
get.description:
Source of the connector's team resources (pkg/connector/team.go:60). Unpaginated — Pulumi returns the full set in one response, and the connector returns an empty page token.

`name` is the connector's team resource ID and the `teamName` path parameter for getTeam and updateTeam — parity-critical.

This listing carries a `members` array in Pulumi's schema, but the connector ignores it here and re-fetches each team via getTeam to build membership grants.

get.summary: Get a team, including its members
get.description:
Called once per team to build membership grants (pkg/connector/team.go:96). `members[].githubLogin` is the join key back to the user resource — parity-critical.

Pulumi's `members` entries also carry a per-team `role` of `admin` or `member`; the connector's `UserInfo` struct does not declare it, so every team membership is emitted as a flat `member` grant and team admins are indistinguishable from team members.

Pulumi returns `listMembersError` when it cannot reach a GitHub- or GitLab-backed team's upstream. The connector does not decode that field, so such a team syncs as having no members rather than surfacing the error.

patch.summary: Add or remove a team member
patch.description:
Backs team membership grant and revoke (pkg/connector/team.go:129 and :146). The connector sends only the `member` and `memberAction` fields.

Pulumi's update-team route is multi-purpose — the same body also carries stack and environment permission edits and team renames. The connector uses none of those, and the spec models only the two fields it sends.

Pulumi accepts `promote` and `demote` alongside `add` and `remove`; the connector never sends them, which is consistent with it not modelling per-team roles in getTeam.

400.description: Teams are not available to individual organizations.

pulumiToken.name: Authorization
pulumiToken.description: A Pulumi access token, sent as `token <access-token>`. The scheme keyword is the literal `token`, not `Bearer`, so this is modelled as an apiKey header rather than an http security scheme.

OrgName.name: orgName
OrgName.description: Organization name. Fixed for the lifetime of the connector by its organization config field.

UserLogin.name: userLogin
UserLogin.description: The member's login name — `user.githubLogin` from listOrganizationMembers, which is also the connector's user resource ID.

TeamName.name: teamName
TeamName.description: Team name — `name` from listTeams, which is also the connector's team resource ID.

continuationToken.description: Opaque cursor for the next page. Absent on the final page, which is what terminates the connector's loop.

OrganizationMember.description: A member of the organization. Only the properties the connector decodes are listed.

role.description:
The member's organization role. Drives the `admin` / `member` entitlement: the connector maps exactly `admin` to the admin entitlement and treats everything else as `member`, so the remaining enum values collapse into `member`.

Pulumi marks this property deprecated in favour of `fgaRole`, which is authoritative for organizations using custom roles — for those members `role` is only the closest built-in projection. The connector reads the deprecated field.

created.description: When the member joined the organization. Decoded into a plain Go string, not a time.

knownToPulumi.description: Whether the member has a Pulumi account. Decoded but not acted on — the connector marks every user ENABLED regardless.

virtualAdmin.description: Decoded by the connector but absent from Pulumi's published schema. Unproven: neither its presence nor its meaning is documented. Not acted on.

UserInfo.description: Display information for a user. Pulumi also returns `email` here on selected endpoints; the connector does not decode it.

githubLogin.description: Login name. The connector's user resource ID, its user-trait login, and the `userLogin` path parameter for writes — parity-critical.

name.description: Display name. The connector falls back to `githubLogin` when this is empty.

avatarUrl.description: Avatar image URL. Decoded but unused.

Team.description: A Pulumi team. Only the properties the connector decodes are listed.

name.description: Unique team name within the organization. The connector's team resource ID and the `teamName` path parameter — parity-critical.

displayName.description: Human-readable name shown in the Pulumi console.

description.description: Free-form description of the team's purpose.

kind.description: Where the team's membership is managed. Decoded but not acted on — the connector writes membership the same way regardless, which will not hold for `github` or `scim` teams whose membership lives upstream.

members.description: Team members. Populated on getTeam; the connector ignores the copy returned by listTeams.

userRole.description: The *calling* user's role on this team, not a property of the team itself. Decoded by the connector but unused; reading it as a team attribute would be a mistake.

UpdateMemberRoleRequest.description: Body of updateOrganizationMemberRole. The client builds it as a map[string]string with a single key.

role.description: The role to assign. The connector sends only `admin` or `member`.

UpdateTeamMembershipRequest.description: Body of updateTeamMembership. The client builds it as a map[string]string with exactly these two keys.

member.description: Login name of the user to add or remove — the connector's user resource ID.

memberAction.description: The action to perform. The connector sends only `add` or `remove`; Pulumi also accepts `promote` and `demote`.
